_comment: Ratchet config for scripts/codecharta-ratchet.py, run against the CodeCharta map (tempus.cc.json.gz). Three gates: (1) per-file aggregate complexity, (2) per-FUNCTION complexity (not gameable by moving code between files), (3) hotspot (complex AND under-tested). Every number below was MEASURED on this repository at v0.19.0 — none was carried over from another project. Ratchet by LOWERING the numbers as the code improves; RAISING a baseline entry needs review justification.

complexity._default_cap_note: Per-file SUM of function complexity. Every file not listed below must stay <= this. The measured median across the 42 non-test Go files is 10 and the highest non-baseline file is domain/belt.go at 25, so 25 is generous for an ordinary file while making an unusually complex NEW file require a reviewed config entry. This gate can be satisfied by splitting a file (the sum moves with the code) — see function_complexity for the ceiling that cannot.

function_complexity._default_cap_note: The single most complex FUNCTION in a file (McCabe). This is the real overall-complexity control: a function keeps its complexity wherever it lives, so moving it between files cannot game this gate — passing requires actually simplifying the function or extracting cohesive sub-functions. Measured: only two files exceed 10 today (baselined below); domain/koppen.go sits exactly at 10.

hotspot._note: A file is a hotspot when it is complex AND under-tested; a NEW hotspot fails the build. The two files below are the measured current ones and are grandfathered — they are visible test debt, not an exemption. Remove them from 'allow' as their coverage improves; the ratchet prints a notice once a file no longer qualifies.
